title: SDK Ops Guardrails & Runloop Lab — Draft
purpose: Short experiment-led playbook for designing developer-facing SDK guardrails (safety, telemetry, retry semantics) and an executable 90-minute lab to validate runloop behavior in realistic dev workflows. This doc is intentionally lightweight — notes, experiments, unresolved questions, and quick checklists for an eng-developer-experience pairing session.
audience: SDK engineers, SDK PMs, developer-experience engineers, solutions engineers running customer pilots.
context: We want SDKs that make it hard for user apps to shoot themselves in the foot (excessive cost, accidental synchronous blocking, silent failures). This lab explores simple defaults + telemetry contracts so that: a) developer-first UX remains frictionless, b) platform can surface actionable signals to ops/console.
what is a \"runloop\" here: The local develop-test-prod cycle where a developer iterates on prompts, runs integration tests, and ramps traffic. Key properties: local dev with low quotas, CI that mocks latency/cost, and canary rollouts that exercise fallback rules.
90-minute lab plan (goal: validate 3 gua:
- Prep (10m): clone sample repo (link in linked_artifacts), install SDK branch with runloop-instrumentation flag.
- Phase A—Cost spike guardrail (20m): craft a batch of prompt-heavy calls, assert SDK enforces a per-request token cap and emits a telemetry event when auto-truncation occurs.
  - Success signal: telemetry event appears within 10s, console shows a per-request cost warning, and unit tests catch truncated responses.
- Phase B—Latency fallback behavior (25m): simulate backend slow path (latency injection), ensure SDK cancels/short-circuits according to latency SLO and fires fallback model call (cheaper variant).
  - Success signal: request completes with fallback model id in response metadata; developer-visible retry explanation printed to stdout.
- Phase C—KV-cache replay and mem leak check (20m): run repeated streaming calls with cached prefixes; verify KV hits logged, memory stable across 100 iterations.
  - Success signal: KV hit ratio > 70% and resident memory flat (±5%) after warmup.
- Wrap + notes (15m): capture failures, file follow-ups, update sample repo README.
Telemetry & contract proposals (quick li:
- Event keys (short strings): sdk.cost.truncation, sdk.latency.fallback, sdk.kv.hit, sdk.kv.miss, sdk.request.canceled
- Minimal payload (per event): request_id, sdk_version, model_id, route, timestamp, local_env (dev|ci|prod), numeric tokens_consumed where relevant
- Where it lives: SDK emits to user telemetry sink (stdout JSON in dev), and platform ingestion hooks when run under authenticated environment. Telemetry must be PII-free.
- Sampling policy: capture every sdk.latency.fallback and sdk.cost.truncation event; sample 1% for sdk.kv.hit in high-traffic labs.
Guardrail candidates (prioritized for la:
1) Token-cap auto-truncation with explicit reason string and event (low friction, immediate cost control)
2) Latency SLO enforcement + model fallback chain (pluggable fallbacks, opt-out via config)
3) Automatic retry backoff + jitter for transient 5xx errors (limit to avoid burst cost)
4) Default safe-serialization for function/tool calling (reject binary blobs > X bytes)
5) Local dev quotas (soft limits) that can be escalated in CI via env var
Developer UX rules-of-thumb:
- Prefer explicit, discoverable warnings over silent mitigation. If we change responses (truncate/fallback), return an explanation field in response and log an event.
- Provide one-line opt-out flags for each guardrail (e.g., SDK_GUARDRAIL_TRUNCATION=off) for advanced users.
- Keep default behavior opinionated and safe — most first-time users should be protected.
Testing checklist (CI + local):
- Unit: guarantee event keys are emitted when corresponding branches hit.
- Integration: runlab script that toggles latency injection and asserts fallback path used.
- Load: synthetic token-heavy batch to validate token-cap behavior and measure CPU/GPU counts (sanity only).
Observability notes (Console + SDK):
- Console: surface aggregated rates (truncation rate, fallback rate) per route and by SDK version.
- SDK: structured JSON lines (one event per line) in dev; integrate with debug logger mode.
- Alerting: create low-noise alerts for sudden spikes in sdk.latency.fallback (e.g., 5x baseline in 10m).
Failure modes and recovery:
- Silent truncation: bad — always emit event and include response.explanation. Recovery: quick rollback option in SDK config.
- Excessive fallbacks: could mask model degradations. Recovery: auto-open a regression eval ticket with sample prompts.
- Telemetry overload: when labs spike, implement sampling and ephemeral backpressure to telemetry sink.
Open questions / TODOs:
- Should the SDK include a local telemetry aggregator (small process) to avoid noisy stdout parsing in labs? (Pros: structured capture; Cons: adds complexity)
- How to handle private deployments where telemetry ingestion is disabled? Propose local file-backed capture + manual upload flow.
- Decide default token cap values per model-size class (tiny/small/medium/large).
- Add a small set of canonical troubleshooting commands to README for engineers running the lab.

notes_to_self: Keep the lab lean and reproducible. Focus on signals we can act on (telemetry + console) rather than perfect mitigation logic. Iterate with solutions engineering — run the lab once with one customer pilot before broad rollout.
